description: This course covers programming fundamentals for cybersecurity, focusing on secure coding practices, cryptography, and network protocols. Topics include secure software development principles, C and Python programming for security analysis, cryptographic algorithms such as AES and RSA, secure communication protocols like TLS/SSL, and ethical hacking techniques. The course also explores malware analysis, reverse engineering, and secure data storage methods. Students will study buffer overflow vulnerabilities, SQL injection, and cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, and learn to implement defensive strategies using tools like Wireshark, GDB, and OpenSSL. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on application of programming concepts to real-world security scenarios, ensuring students can develop and analyze secure systems using industry-standard practices and frameworks.

clos.text: Define secure coding practices and their role in preventing common vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows and SQL injection.
Describe cryptographic algorithms including AES, RSA, and SHA-256, and their implementation in Python using libraries like PyCryptodome.
Explain network protocols such as TLS/SSL and their application in secure communication using Wireshark for packet analysis.
Apply secure programming techniques to develop applications that resist common cyber threats using C and Python.
Implement defensive measures against malware and exploit techniques using reverse engineering tools like GDB and IDA Pro.
